content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

OpenAI added two image models, GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst and GPT-Image-2.6 Flare, to its API on November 4, 2026, according to the [API changelog](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog), which lists adjustable complexity, SVG generation and animated GIF generation, and says markup-guided editing was added for supported GPT-Image-2.5 and GPT-Image-2.6 models. The release accompanies Images 2.6 in ChatGPT, which [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1...

editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Claim-accuracy tests run from raw text. (a) Preview claim: the API reference does say 'Requires access to the GIF preview for the selected model.' and no other cited page (guide, both 2.6 model pages, changelog, launch post) mentions a preview or an access requirement for GIF output (grep of the guide: no 'preview' at all; 'early access customers' in the launch post refers to launch customers, not API access). The headline claim stands, attributed to the reference. Subordinate imprecision: the sentence sits in the frame_count entry, and the other pages are silent rather than contradicting it, so 'pages differ on GIF access' is slightly stronger than 'silent' (clarification filed). (b) Batch claim: verified for both Sunburst and Flare 2.6 pages ('Not supported'), versus 'Supported' on 2.5 Sunburst, 2.5 Flare and gpt-image-2; pricing Batch table has no 2.6 rows; the article labels this 'the Herald's comparison of the pages' and adds that the launch post does not mention Batch. Quantifier 'the 2.6 model pages' covers exactly the two 2.6 pages cited. (c) Dates: November 4, 2026 is the changelog entry date, matched by the launch post date, MarkTechPost's date and The Verge's 6:00 PM UTC timestamp; no time-zone conflict. Deprecation entry dated 2026-11-10 is on the deprecations page (not the changelog), as the article says; removal February 10, 2027; Dec 1, 2026 removals attributed to the June 2 notice. (d) Disagreement: guide 20-2000 ms versus reference minimum 20 with a 655,350 ms cap on the encoded delay; no source explains it; the article reports both and says the Herald does not reconcile them, as policy requires. (e) Speed figures: labelled as OpenAI's, relayed by MarkTechPost, with no baseline named; 'none of the three outlets reports a measurement' holds against The Verge, MarkTechPost and TechRadar (the quantifier was checked against all three; no outlet cites a measured time). (f) Absence/quantifier regex run: 'both models use high', 'both models support', 'all subscription levels', 'neither ... nor', 'only MarkTechPost covers the API in detail' (The Verge has a single API sentence, so 'in detail' is a correct qualifier), 'none of the three outlets': all hold. (g) Derived figures: no Herald-computed counts or sums. (h) Independence: not an Analysis, so no independent-source minimum; 11 of 14 sources are OpenAI's own and the three outlets are described as ChatGPT-focused (Verge, TechRadar) and as restating OpenAI's docs (MarkTechPost). (i) Body URLs and the sources array match exactly (14 each, none orphaned); The Decoder is not cited.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Vendor claims are attributed to OpenAI; the Herald's own comparisons are labelled; no promotional language, no AI self-reference, no speculation (the closing section lists what is not established).
editor_notes.originality: New topic: no published article covers GPT-Image models, Images 2.5/2.6 or the OpenAI image API (searched articles and article-meta in 2026-09 to 2026-11); no open PR duplicates it (open PRs 2852, 2853 are on other subjects).
concerns: The 'Requires access to the GIF preview' sentence appears only in the reference's frame_count entry, and the other pages are silent rather than contradictory; the headline, summary and 'Where OpenAI's pages differ' section present it as a page-level difference in GIF access (clarification filed).

The MarkTechPost page could not be snapshotted (403) and was read through a reader proxy because Archive.org holds no capture; the article's MarkTechPost statements were all confirmed against that raw text.

The writer's statement that the launch post's live page did not load for the Herald's fetcher is not true of the reviewer's fetch; it concerns the writer's process, not a claim about the subject, and the article discloses the Archive.org route.
recommendations: When a documentation claim sits in a single parameter entry, say which parameter carries it.
Say 'silent' rather than 'differ' when the other pages simply do not mention a restriction.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped News coverage of a vendor API release whose documentation disagrees with itself in several checkable places; the 148-character headline's two claims about OpenAI's documentation are both supported by raw page text, with a small location and framing clarification filed. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS (one clarification record).
